title: The Tricky Wolf and the Rats
author: Ellen C. Babbitt
summary: 狼装瘸骗老鼠，鼠首领识破后咬死了它。
publicDomainBasis: Retold by Ellen C. Babbitt and published in 1922 by The Century Co. (pre-1923, public domain in the United States); Project Gutenberg releases it as public domain.

paragraphs.en: Once upon a time a Big Rat lived in the forest, and many hundreds of other Rats called him their Chief.
paragraphs.zh: 从前，森林里住着一只大老鼠，几百只别的老鼠都称它为首领。

paragraphs.en: A Tricky Wolf saw this troop of Rats, and began to plan how he could catch them. He wanted to eat them, but how was he to get them? At last he thought of a plan. He went to a corner near the home of the Rats and waited until he saw one of them coming. Then he stood up on his hind legs.
paragraphs.zh: 一只狡猾的狼看见这群老鼠，便开始盘算怎么抓住它们。它想吃掉它们，可怎么才能弄到手呢？最后它想出一个主意。它来到老鼠住处附近的一个角落，等着，直到看见一只老鼠走过来。然后它用后腿站了起来。

paragraphs.en: The Chief of the Rats said to the Wolf, "Wolf, why do you stand on your hind legs?"
paragraphs.zh: 鼠首领对狼说：“狼，你为什么用后腿站着？”

paragraphs.en: "Because I am lame," said the Tricky Wolf. "It hurts me to stand on my front legs."
paragraphs.zh: “因为我瘸了，”狡猾的狼说，“用前腿站着疼。”

paragraphs.en: "And why do you keep your mouth open?" asked the Rat.

"I keep my mouth open so that I may drink in all the air I can," said the Wolf. "I live on air; it is my only food day after day. I can not run or walk, so I stay here. I try not to complain." When the Rats went away the Wolf lay down.
paragraphs.zh: “我张着嘴，好多吸些空气，”狼说，“我靠空气活着；一天又一天，这是我唯一的食物。我不能跑也不能走，所以就待在这儿。我尽量不抱怨。”老鼠们走后，狼就趴下了。

paragraphs.en: The Chief of the Rats was sorry for the Wolf, and he went each night and morning with all the other Rats to talk with the Wolf, who seemed so poor, and who did not complain.
paragraphs.zh: 鼠首领很可怜这只狼，便每天早晚带着所有老鼠去跟狼说话，那狼看上去那么可怜，又不抱怨。

paragraphs.en: Each time as the Rats were leaving, the Wolf caught and ate the last one. Then he wiped his lips, and looked as if nothing had happened.
paragraphs.zh: 每次老鼠们离开时，狼就抓住最后一只吃掉。然后它舔舔嘴唇，装出什么也没发生的样子。

paragraphs.en: Each night there were fewer Rats at bedtime. Then they asked the Chief of the Rats what the trouble was. He could not be sure, but he thought the Wolf was to blame.
paragraphs.zh: 每天晚上来睡觉的老鼠越来越少。于是它们问鼠首领出了什么事。它不能确定，但觉得该怪那只狼。

paragraphs.en: So the next day the Chief said to the other Rats, "You go first this time and I will go last."
paragraphs.zh: 于是第二天，鼠首领对别的老鼠说：“这次你们先走，我走最后。”

paragraphs.en: They did so, and as the Chief of the Rats went by, the Wolf made a spring at him. But the Wolf was not quick enough, and the Chief of the Rats got away.
paragraphs.zh: 它们照办了。鼠首领经过时，狼朝它扑了过去。可狼不够快，鼠首领逃掉了。

paragraphs.en: "So this is the food you eat. Your legs are not so lame as they were. You have played your last trick, Wolf," said the Chief of the Rats, springing at the Wolf's throat. He bit the Wolf, so that he died.
paragraphs.zh: “原来你吃的是这个。你的腿可没先前那么瘸了。你的把戏耍到头了，狼。”鼠首领说着，扑向狼的喉咙。它咬死了狼。

paragraphs.en: And ever after the Rats lived happily in peace and quiet.
paragraphs.zh: 从此以后，老鼠们过着快乐安宁的日子。
